title: Marshmallow & Spaghetti Tower
hypothesis: I thought I could build a super tall tower using marshmallows as the corners.
observation: I poked spaghetti into marshmallows to make triangles, then stacked them up high! The triangles kept it from wobbling. My tower ended up taller than my teddy bear!
funFact: Engineers use triangle shapes in bridges and towers because a triangle is the strongest, steadiest shape.

title: The Walking Rainbow Water
hypothesis: I thought the colored water would climb up the paper towels and mix together to make brand new colors.
observation: The water slowly walked up the paper towels into the empty cups! Red and yellow made orange, and blue and yellow made green — like magic!
funFact: Water can climb uphill through tiny tubes in the paper. Scientists call this 'capillary action'.

title: The Erupting Kitchen Volcano!
hypothesis: If I pour vinegar onto the baking soda, it will fizz up and bubble over like a real volcano.
observation: It instantly bubbled up and overflowed like hot red lava! I chased the foam all across the counter while Dad cheered.
funFact: The fizzy bubbles are a gas called carbon dioxide — the very same gas that makes soda pop fizzy!

title: Light-Up Lego Spaceship
hypothesis: If I connect the battery to the tiny bulb with copper tape, the light will turn on.
observation: We taped the wires to the battery and the LED glowed bright yellow! We built it right into the cockpit of my Lego space shuttle so it shines in the dark.
funFact: Electricity has to travel in a complete loop called a 'circuit'. If there is a gap, the light won't glow.

title: The Floating Salt-Water Egg
hypothesis: I thought both eggs would sink straight down, because eggs are heavy.
observation: The egg in plain water sank to the bottom, but the egg in the salty water floated right at the top! The salt made the water stronger.
funFact: Salt water is denser (more packed) than plain water, so it can hold heavier things up — that's why it's easy to float in the ocean!

title: Growing a Bean Seed
hypothesis: I thought if I keep the bean wet and sunny, a little plant would pop out.
observation: After a few days a white root wiggled out, and then a tiny green leaf popped up! I watered it every morning and watched it grow bigger and bigger.
funFact: A seed already has a baby plant tucked inside — it just needs water, warmth, and light to wake up!
